name: ftu-model-coverage
title: FTU Model Coverage — Do Existing BioModels Model HRA Functional Tissue Units?
question:
Do existing BioModels model HRA functional tissue units (FTUs) -- Katy
Boerner's question -- and, for the FTUs that already have models, can HRA
CTpop (Cell Type Populations) cell-type counts parameterize them, per the
RUI -> CTpop -> model vision Peter Hunter and SPARC-heart describe?

study_card.goal: Match the committed full-corpus BioModels catalog's model names against a curated list of 11 HRA functional tissue units (pancreatic islet, kidney glomerulus/nephron, liver lobule, lung alveolus, colon crypt, small-intestine crypt-villus axis, cardiac muscle unit, ovarian follicle, skin epidermis unit, lymph node follicle) by synonym substring, and stub the CTpop -> model parameterization seam for a covered FTU (e.g. the islet).
study_card.mechanism: FtuModelCoverageStep.update -> build_ftu_model_coverage(catalog_path) -> load_corpus_catalog(datasets/biomodel_corpus_catalog.json) x HRA_FTUS synonym substring match against each biomodel_do's name -> ftu_coverage rows (n_models/model_ids/covered per FTU) + summary -> RAMEmitter. ctpop_parameter_stub(ftu_name) separately returns a covered FTU's cell types as candidate CTpop-parameterizable inputs (v1 stub, no real CTpop count bound yet).
study_card.expected_result: At least a few well-studied FTUs (pancreatic islet, colon crypt, cardiac muscle) already have multiple curated models; several other FTUs (kidney glomerulus/nephron, lung alveolus, small-intestine villus, ovarian follicle, lymph node follicle) have none in the current corpus, at name-matching granularity.
study_card.main_expert_question: For the FTUs that already have models (islet, liver lobule, colon crypt, cardiac muscle, skin epidermis), which of those models' parameters are actually cell-population-scale (vs. single-cell-only), i.e. genuinely CTpop-parameterizable, and would a real CTpop count binding change their calibration?

biological_summary:
Katy Boerner's question for the HRA-3D track was whether the mechanistic-
modeling literature (as indexed by BioModels) already tries to model
functional tissue units -- the sub-organ, cell-population-scale structures
(e.g. a single pancreatic islet, a single nephron) that sit between whole-
organ models and single-cell models, and that Peter Hunter/SPARC's
RUI -> CTpop -> model vision targets for parameterization. Crossing the
full 1,096-model curated corpus against a curated 11-FTU list finds real
hits: the pancreatic islet (3 models -- Jiang2007's GSIS beta-cell system,
Bertram2007's islet-cell oscillations, Wierschem2004's islet electrical
bursting), the colon crypt (4 models -- Smallbone2013's Colon Crypt cycle,
versions 0-3), the cardiac muscle/myocardium unit (3 models -- Cooling2007's
cardiac-myocyte IP3 transients, McDougal2017's ischemic-cardiomyocyte
metabolism, Zhou2024's post-infarction myocyte electromechanics -- directly
relevant to the SPARC-heart use case), the liver lobule (2 models -- both
hepatocyte-scale), and the skin epidermis unit (1 model, Cursons2015's
epidermal ERK-MAPK regulation). Six of the 11 curated FTUs (kidney
glomerulus, kidney nephron, lung alveolus, small-intestine crypt-villus
axis, ovarian follicle, lymph node follicle) match no model in the current
corpus at this name-matching granularity. For the covered FTUs, this study
also stubs the CTpop parameterization seam: HRA CTpop (Bueckle 2026) gives
per-anatomical-structure cell-type counts/proportions for a RUI-registered
tissue block, which would set an FTU model's cell-population parameters --
e.g. an islet's measured beta/alpha/delta-cell counts binding the
Jiang2007/Bertram2007 islet models' beta-cell-mass parameters. `
ctpop_parameter_stub` identifies which cell types are the candidate
parameterization targets; it does not yet bind a real CTpop count.
readouts: ftu_coverage_summary.n_models_matched (distinct corpus models matched to at least one FTU)
ctpop_parameter_stub(ftu).cell_types (candidate CTpop-parameterizable inputs for a covered FTU)

report.title: FTU Model Coverage — 5/11 curated FTUs covered (13 models); islet/crypt/cardiac-muscle best-covered
report.objective:
Do existing BioModels model HRA functional tissue units, and can HRA
CTpop cell-type counts parameterize the covered ones?
report.conclusion:
Crossing the full 1,096-model committed corpus catalog
(`datasets/biomodel_corpus_catalog.json`) against a curated 11-FTU list
by name/synonym substring match, 5/11 FTUs (45.5%) are covered by at
least one model, matching 13 distinct models total
(`n_models_matched`): pancreatic islet of Langerhans (3 models --
Jiang2007 GSIS, Bertram2007 islet-cell oscillations, Wierschem2004
islet electrical bursting), colon crypt of Lieberkuhn (4 models --
Smallbone2013 Colon Crypt cycle versions 0-3), cardiac muscle/
myocardium unit (3 models -- Cooling2007, McDougal2017, Zhou2024,
directly SPARC-heart-relevant), liver lobule (2 models), and skin
epidermis unit (1 model, Cursons2015). Six FTUs -- kidney glomerulus,
kidney nephron, lung alveolus, small-intestine crypt-villus axis,
ovarian follicle, lymph node follicle -- match zero models in the
current corpus at this granularity. So: yes, existing BioModels do
model several HRA FTUs already, answering Katy Boerner's question in
the affirmative for at least these five, while confirming real gaps
elsewhere. `ctpop_parameter_stub("pancreatic islet of Langerhans")`
confirms the islet's beta/alpha/delta cell types (CL:0000169/0171/0173)
as the candidate CTpop-parameterizable inputs for the islet models
above, stubbing (not yet implementing) the RUI -> CTpop -> model
parameterization seam.
report.caveat:
Coverage is name/synonym substring matching against the biomodel-DO
catalog's `name` field only, not curated per-model FTU annotation or
model-content inspection -- a model whose title omits the FTU synonym
but whose equations genuinely operate at FTU scale would be a false
negative (undercounting), and a model whose title happens to contain a
synonym for an unrelated reason would be a false positive
(overcounting); neither is checked against actual model structure here.
The CTpop parameterization seam is a v1 stub: it identifies candidate
cell-type parameters, it does not bind any real CTpop cell-type count
to a specific model parameter, so `pipeline_gate.gate_evaluator.result`
is `needs_calibration`.

findings.statement:
Crossing the full 1,096-model curated BioModels corpus against a
curated 11-FTU list by name/synonym substring match covers 5/11 FTUs
(45.5%), matching 13 distinct models: pancreatic islet of Langerhans
(3 models), colon crypt of Lieberkuhn (4 models, all Smallbone2013
Colon Crypt cycle versions), cardiac muscle/myocardium unit (3
models, SPARC-heart-relevant), liver lobule (2 models), and skin
epidermis unit (1 model). Six FTUs (kidney glomerulus, kidney
nephron, lung alveolus, small-intestine crypt-villus axis, ovarian
follicle, lymph node follicle) match zero models -- existing
BioModels do already model several HRA FTUs, but real modeling
white-space remains for the rest.

evidence.summary: 5/11 FTUs covered (45.5%), 13 distinct models matched: islet=3 (Jiang2007, Bertram2007, Wierschem2004), colon crypt=4 (Smallbone2013 v0-v3), cardiac muscle=3 (Cooling2007, McDougal2017, Zhou2024), liver lobule=2, skin epidermis=1; 0 for glomerulus/nephron/alveolus/villus/ovarian follicle/lymph node follicle.

regression_compatibility.basis: The baseline ftu-model-coverage composite (committed catalog x curated HRA_FTUS list) completed without error, emitting a non-empty ftu_coverage list and summary.

biological_validation.basis: Coverage is name/synonym substring matching (not curated per-model FTU annotation or model-content inspection) and the CTpop parameterization seam is a v1 stub with no real cell-type count bound to any model parameter yet, so gated needs_calibration rather than passed -- but the underlying model hits (islet, colon crypt, cardiac muscle, liver lobule, skin epidermis) are real, named, resolvable BioModels IDs.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-01 directly answers Katy Boerner's question -- yes, existing BioModels do model several HRA FTUs already (5/11, 13 models) -- while also enumerating the six FTUs with zero current coverage, the study's central interpretive claim.

limitations: Coverage is name/synonym substring matching against the catalog's `name` field only -- no per-model FTU annotation or model-equation inspection, so both false negatives (FTU-scale models whose title omits the synonym) and false positives (incidental name matches) are possible and unchecked.

The CTpop parameterization seam (`ctpop_parameter_stub`) is a v1 stub: it identifies which of an FTU's cell types are candidate CTpop-parameterizable inputs, it does not bind any real per-structure CTpop cell-type count to a specific model parameter.
The curated 11-FTU list (`HRA_FTUS`) is hand-curated, not pulled live from an HRA FTU digital-object registry -- it may omit FTUs the HRA itself catalogs.

resolved_uncertainties: Existing BioModels do already model several HRA FTUs at real, named-model granularity -- pancreatic islet (3), colon crypt (4), cardiac muscle/myocardium (3), liver lobule (2), skin epidermis (1) -- directly answering Katy Boerner's question in the affirmative for these five.

The islet's characteristic cell types (beta/alpha/delta, CL:0000169/0171/0173) are identifiable as candidate CTpop-parameterizable inputs for the covered islet models, confirming the RUI -> CTpop -> model parameterization seam is at least well-defined for a covered FTU.
remaining_uncertainties: Six FTUs (kidney glomerulus, kidney nephron, lung alveolus, small-intestine crypt-villus axis, ovarian follicle, lymph node follicle) have zero matching models at this granularity -- is that a real modeling gap, or a name-matching recall failure?

Does binding a REAL HRA CTpop cell-type count (not just identifying candidate cell types) to the Topp2000/Jiang2007/Bertram2007 islet models' beta-cell-mass parameters materially change their calibration?

followup_study_proposals.title: Bind HRA CTpop islet cell counts to the islet-model parameters
followup_study_proposals.motivation: ctpop_parameter_stub identifies the islet's beta/alpha/delta cell types as candidate CTpop-parameterizable inputs but binds no real count; a real RUI-registered islet's measured cell-type proportions would let the Topp2000/Jiang2007/Bertram2007 islet models be re-parameterized against actual measured tissue composition rather than literature-default beta-cell-mass values.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Fetch a real HRA CTpop result for a RUI-registered pancreatic-islet tissue block (per-anatomical-structure beta/alpha/delta-cell counts/proportions), map those counts onto the Topp2000/Jiang2007/Bertram2007 islet models' beta-cell-mass (or equivalent cell-population) parameters, and compare simulated output against the models' literature-default parameterization.
